subject: Dat aSwift production: sustained p99 latency + 5xx spike — requesting urgent remediation
messages:
From: Amandeep Singh <amandeep@dataswift.ai>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: DataSwift SRE Team <sre@dataswift.ai>
Date: 2027-08-14T09:12:00Z
Subject: Production: sustained p99 latency + 5xx spike

Hi Soojin,

We're seeing a marked regression in our production traffic since ~08:40 UTC. P99 latency for text-generation calls has climbed from ~180ms to ~1.7s and a small but growing fraction of requests are returning 502/504. This is impacting our autocomplete and search features (affects ~6% of user sessions).

Attached is a 60m trace (dataswift_p99_graph_20270814.png) and a small sample of error payloads. Our SREs flagged unusual queue growth on hot-lane workers and repeated cache eviction logs. Can Redwood advise immediate mitigations? We have a major marketing campaign starting Monday; this is blocking.

Thanks,
Amandeep
Head of Platform — DataSwift

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-14T09:41:00Z
Subject: Re: Production: sustained p99 latency + 5xx spike

Folks — quick notes from the infra investigation (observed 09:35 UTC):
- Hot-lane queue depth on a subset of GPU pools (hot-lane-3a, hot-lane-3b) is elevated, with long tail waits.
- KV cache eviction rate jumped ~6x at ~08:37 UTC. Eviction logs show aggressive TTL trimming and a concurrent re-population storm.
- Batch lane timeouts are set to 20ms for this tenant; with the recent traffic burst that increases head-of-line (HOL) blocking when a large request touches a hot prefix.
- There's evidence of prefix misallocation: certain tenant keys are concentrated on 2 physical workers due to an earlier rebalance that didn't fully rehash.

Temporary mitigations I recommend now (can push in 10–15m):
1) Increase per-tenant batch timeout to 50ms (reduces HOL probability).
2) Reduce KV eviction aggressiveness for the next 30 minutes (increase cache capacity for tenant namespace).
3) Trigger a soft rehash of prefix mapping for affected pools to spread hot prefixes.

I’ll coordinate with SRE to roll 1–2 in a canary first. If accepted, we should see p99 come down within one batch cycle (~2–3 minutes).

Ben
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

(attachment: runbook_kv_tuning_v2.pdf)

From: Amandeep Singh <amandeep@dataswift.ai>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: DataSwift SRE Team <sre@dataswift.ai>
Date: 2027-08-14T09:58:00Z
Subject: Re: Production: sustained p99 latency + 5xx spike

Ben — thanks, that matches what our SREs are seeing. We did a small traffic shift at 07:45 UTC (routing a campaign traffic slice to the Redwood hosted endpoint) but we did not change model pins or batching. The campaign traffic is short-tenured but high concurrency bursts (search autocompete + suggestions).

Please push the suggested mitigations; we’re happy for a canary on a single pool first. Also, any temporary fallbacks (e.g., route to a slightly lower-capacity model with more even sharding) that reduce user-visible errors are acceptable for the next 24h.

Amandeep

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, ceo@redwood.com <ceo@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-16T16:43:00Z
Subject: Re: Production: sustained p99 latency + 5xx spike — postmortem and next steps

Quick postmortem summary for leadership and DataSwift execs (short version):
- Root cause: a short, high-concurrency traffic spike from a marketing campaign exposed a concentration of hot prefixes combined with aggressive KV eviction TTLs and a low batch-timeout configuration. The interaction produced HOL blocking on a small set of hot-lane workers and a re-population thrash that produced transient 5xxs.
- Immediate mitigations applied (08/14 09:55 UTC): increased batch timeout to 50ms for tenant, reduced eviction aggressiveness, and soft-rehashed prefix mapping. P99 dropped from ~1.7s to ~220ms within 3 minutes; 5xx rate returned to baseline over 12 minutes.
- Action items (owner / ETA):
  * Complete a permanent prefix rebalancer to avoid single-worker concentration — owner: Infra (Ben) / ETA: 2027-08-21
  * Add adaptive batch-timeout heuristic based on queue depth — owner: Runtime team / ETA: 2027-09-02
  * Tenant-level cache sizing recommendations surfaced to account teams during onboarding — owner: Solutions (Marissa) / ETA: 2027-08-28
  * Add tenant traffic-shift safety guardrails (auto-fallback routing to compatible model variants) — owner: Product (Jonas) / ETA: 2027-09-10

I’ll share the longer write-up and the metrics dashboard link to the Drive folder. We should also offer DataSwift a 10% credit on August usage for the customer experience impact (pending sales approval).

Jonas Weber
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference
